question: to the Commission Jean-Paul Garraud (PfE) Subject:

In certain ‘exceptional’ situations, the Commission may propose measures that are then decided by the governments of the Member States, without the European Parliament being fully involved in their adoption. This emergency mechanism should not become a standard way of excluding the representatives elected by the citizens. In recent years, using exceptional instruments in areas such as health, energy, the internal market and defence has led to an increased use of derogation procedures. While these mechanisms may be justified in certain circumstances, they should not lead to long-term weakening of the European Parliament’s role in EU policy-making or to making trivial use of exception procedures. 1.

In what specific situations does the Commission consider that it can propose a measure without going through the normal legislative procedure involving the European Parliament, and what objective criteria make it possible to characterise an emergency that warrants use of such a procedure?

Does the Commission undertake to explain publicly, for each emergency measure, why Parliament cannot be involved in the decision, by publishing a detailed statement of reasons demonstrating that use of that procedure is necessary and proportionate?
Does it agree that these measures should always be limited in time and subject to rapid scrutiny by the European Parliament?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (29.9.2026) 1. Article 122 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) sets out the conditions under which this provision can be used as a legal basis. In her political guidelines for 2024-2029, the President of the Commission pledged to ensure that the Commission uses this tool only in exceptional circumstances. This commitment is reflected in point 52 of the revised Framework Agreement on relations between the European Parliament and the European Commission1. It provides that, without prejudice to any other procedures provided for in the Treaties, recourse to Article 122 TFEU is only possible on an exceptional basis and under the strict conditions set out in that Article. 2. In line with the commitment in the political guidelines, point 52 of the Framework Agreement also states that the Commission commits to provide without delay comprehensive justification and information on the exceptional and emergency cases where the proposals by the Commission are based on Article 122 TFEU. 3. In addition, point 52 of the Framework Agreement provides that, at the earliest three months after the entry into force of the legal act based on Article 122 TFEU, and at appropriate intervals thereafter, the Member of the Commission responsible shall, at the request of the President of European Parliament, report on the implementation of the legal act concerned, including an assessment of the legal act.
